title: Rapid failover: KV lease contention incident review
content:
Overview:

Summary: On 2029-11-28 at ~02:13 UTC the hosted-api serving plane experienced a P0 degradation characterized by p95/p99 latency spikes and a brief (22m) increase in 5xx for streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Root cause: a cascade of KV cache lease renewals that synchronized across a subset of serving hosts during a scheduled rapid-failover test, which amplified RPC contention to the KV layer and triggered request queuing in the multiplex scheduler.

Impact:
- Affected surface: hosted-api (read-write paths) for eu-west-1 and us-east-1 edge clusters; streaming endpoints saw partial chunking/fragmentation.
- Duration: first symptoms 2029-11-28 02:13 UTC; mitigation reduced severity by 02:28 UTC; full stabilization 02:35 UTC.
- Customer impact: ~18% increase in p99 for generation endpoints during window; ~0.9% overall error rate bump (5xx). Several high-QPS enterprise tenants saw degraded tail latency and reported timeouts from SDK users.

How we detected it:
- Pager triggered by p99 latency SLO alert from hosted-api-frontend (2:15 UTC).
- Oncall automated playbook suggested "check kv lease" after initial telemetry pointed to elevated KV latency.
- SRE oncall (Priya) triaged via dashboards and invoked runbook steps; escalated to core serving runtime and infra teams.

Timeline (high-level):
- 02:09 UTC: Scheduled rapid-failover test kicked off for a subset of edge nodes (intended to exercise our graceful failover path). Test was started by platform-eng (ticket INF-9072).
- 02:13 UTC: Alerting pipeline fires: p99 latency spike on hosted-api-frontend (eu-west-1).
- 02:14 UTC: Oncall confirms elevated KV RPC latencies and KV lease renewal rate spike.
- 02:16 UTC: Observed synchronous lease renewal window: 110 hosts refreshed leases within a ~6s window; KV leader aggregated requests and started queuing.
- 02:18 UTC: Multiplex scheduler queues started to grow; streaming sessions began to fragment (clients saw partial chuncking + reconnects).
- 02:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation: disabled scheduled failover test and incrementally increased KV client parallelism on edge-proxy for affected hosts.
- 02:28 UTC: Latency curves started normalizing; p99 trending down.
- 02:35 UTC: System stabilized. Post-incident monitoring continued for 24h.

Root cause analysis (technical details):
- The rapid-failover test caused many edge hosts to concurrently transition through the same lifecycle hooks (evict->reconnect->lease-renew). Our lease refresh logic has a fallback that, on transient RPC failures, will retry aggressively with fixed timings rather than jittered backoff. When ~100 hosts retried in lockstep, the KV cluster saw a coordinated burst of lease-related RPCs (GetLease / RenewLease) and internal leader election churn increased KV leader CPU and RPC queue length.
- The KV layer (internal service kv-store-v2) uses a leader node that handles lease tokens; it protects correctness but is sensitive to synchronous bursts. The leader-side queuing bumped RPC latency from ~3ms to ~90-200ms during the peak.
- Serving runtime's multiplex scheduler is designed to keep tail latency low by limiting in-flight requests per worker. The scheduler's admission control thresholds were hit due to prolonged KV RPCs, causing backlog and some request timeouts which surfaced as 5xx upstream.

Contributing factors:
1) Test orchestration: failover harness executed lifecycle events without jittering start times across hosts.
2) Lease client implementation: lacks Jittered exponential backoff for renewals; uses fixed multi-retry window that aligns retries.
3) Telemetry gap: KV leader queue depth metric exists but alerting thresholds are conservative; we didn't have a burn-rate or anomaly detector that would have correlated lease renewal spikes with leader CPU increase.
4) Runbook incompleteness: the rapid-failover test is documented in INF-9072 but the interplay with KV lease behavior is not captured in the SRE runbook; oncall guidance lacked an immediate "reduce kv client concurrency" knob.

What we did during the incident (actions and timeline):
- 02:17 UTC: Identified synchronized lease renewals.
- 02:18 UTC: Team disabled the scheduled failover via the test harness (platform-eng).
- 02:20 UTC: Applied emergency tweak: increase KV client concurrency threshold at the edge-proxy to allow more non-blocking requests while leader queues drained (config roll via infra hotpath).
- 02:22 UTC: Added temporary circuit-breaker on renew path to cap retries per second from any single host.
- 02:27 UTC: Began incremental rollback of emergency settings and monitored stability.

Short-term mitigations (post-incident, immediate):
- Push patch to lease client to add jittered retry within 24h (hotfix PR #5372 references).
- Add a temporary alert that correlates lease-refresh-rate with KV-leader-queue-depth (burn-rate style) to detect repeat surges.
- Update the rapid-failover harness to stagger lifecycle events across hosts (config flag: --stagger-seconds).

Long-term remediation (engineering/plans):
- Redesign lease renew path to be token-bucket paced and to use capped exponential backoff + jitter (owner: runtime team, due 2029-12-20).
- KV cluster hardening: add read-replicas for lease checking and implement soft-leases to reduce leader pressure (owner: infra-kv, due 2029-03-01).
- Scheduler resilience: make multiplex admission control resilient to downstream RPC path increases by allowing limited soft-fails and fallback to local cache (owner: serving-runtime, due 2029-01-15).
- Runbook and playbook updates: explicit steps to throttle lease renewal sources, config knobs to immediately reduce kv-client concurrency, and an incident checklist for failover testing (owner: eng-sre, due 2029-12-10).

Runbook gaps discovered:
- No immediate, documented knob for "global lease renew throttle" for emergency use. We added a workaround during the incident but it's manual and error-prone.
- Orchestration tests (failover harness) default to synchronous host transitions; documentation doesn't warn of lease-cluster pressure.
- Alerting correlation missing (we had metrics but not composite alerts tying them into a single severity trigger).

Action items (short, assign, due):
- SRE-01: Update `sre/hostedapi/runbooks/kv-lease.md` with emergency throttle steps and a quick CLI command. Owner: Priya. Due: 2029-12-05.
- SRE-02: Add burn-rate composite alert in PagerDuty for lease-refresh spikes + kv-leader-queue-depth. Owner: Liam. Due: 2029-12-03.
- ENG-01: Runtime patch to add jittered backoff to lease renewals, PR -> review -> ship. Owner: Nadia. Due: 2029-11-30 (hotfix branch).
- ENG-02: Failover harness change to stagger host lifecycle events with random jitter. Owner: Platform-eng (ticket INF-9072). Due: 2029-12-06.
- INF-01: KV infra exploration to add soft-lease support; architecture doc followup. Owner: Omar. Due: 2029-01-31.

Post-incident monitoring plan:
- Maintain elevated telemetry watch for 72 hours on kv-leader-queue-depth, lease-refresh-rate, hosted-api-p99, multiplex-queue-length.
- Weekly verification of failover harness defaults in lower environments.

Appendix / quick diagnostics (commands & dashboards used):
- Dashboards: hosted-api/p99-latency, kv-store-v2/leader-queue, runtime/multiplex-queue
- Kibana query snippets: "lease_renewal_count:>100 AND region:eu-west-1"
- Emergency CLI (internal): infractl kv throttle --set-rate 200/s --scope hostgroup=edge-eu-west-1

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- We should validate whether leader-shipping of lease tokens could be offloaded to a small set of dedicated lease proxies to avoid leader hot paths; would add an extra hop but reduce hotspots.
- Confirm whether other scheduled tests across org use similar synchronous patterns (ask platform-eng for a list).
- Need to add a synthetic test that intentionally exercises staggered renewals to ensure behavior is safe before we re-run the rapid-failover test in prod.

Conclusion:
This incident exposed a classic coupling between orchestration (test harness) behavior and a correctness-oriented central KV service. The immediate customer impact was limited but the tail-latency effect is unacceptable for our hosted customers. The hotfix (jittered backoff) and runbook improvements should reduce recurrence risk; infra-level changes (soft-leases and read-replicas) will be the durable solution.

References:
- Jira: SRE-4821 (incident), INF-9072 (failover harness test ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5372
- Confluence: /display/SRE/kv-lease-runbook
- Slack thread: #oncall-postmortem-threads/Ho8p9

Signed-off-by: Priya Menon (oncall)
